*ReachKit*

## What do you need before you start?

You need a working domain for your business, a few minutes to review results, and a willingness to publish new pages regularly — this isn't a one-time fix. You don't need an SEO background or any technical setup.

Before starting, have ready:

- Your business's domain name.
- A sense of who your real rivals are — the companies buyers compare you against.
- An account you can check weekly, since the work here isn't a single edit but an ongoing publishing habit.

> A free scan shows where AI answers and Google search send buyers to your rivals instead of you. ([reachkit.app](https://reachkit.app/))

[source](https://reachkit.app/)

That scan is the starting point. Everything after it depends on knowing where you stand first — without it, you're choosing what to publish based on guesswork rather than on what AI and Google are showing buyers right now. The scan reads your domain, checks how it turns up (or doesn't) across AI answers and search, and hands back a number you can act on. Skipping that step doesn't save time; it just means the pages that follow aim at the wrong gaps.

## What are the steps to get named in AI answers?

The process runs from measurement to publishing to rechecking, in that order — skip the measurement step and you're guessing at what to write.

1. **Scan your domain.** This takes under a minute and needs no account. It tells you how AI and Google currently find your site, and gives you a starting score — one example scan showed a result of 47/100, described plainly as [hard to find](https://reachkit.app/signin), with the fixes that move it shown alongside.
2. **Pick your market and rivals.** You're asked to confirm or adjust a suggested list of competitors — [the process](https://reachkit.app/) suggests, you confirm, so the comparison matches who buyers weigh you against.
3. **Read your Discoverability Score and AI answers count.** One dashboard view showed a score of 62, up 8 points that week, with AI answers at 2 out of 12 checked — a concrete read on how often your business turns up versus how often it could.
4. **Let pages get written for your market's real questions.** ReachKit finds the questions your market asks that name rivals and not you, writes a page that answers each one from facts on your own site, and publishes it on your schedule — see [reachkit.app](https://reachkit.app/).
5. **Review each page before it goes live.** Every page waits a day for you to read it — or stop it — before it goes live, so nothing publishes without your say. [source](https://reachkit.app/)
6. **Let pages go live on your domain.** Pages go live on your domain, and you get 24 hours to stop it — a fixed window, not an open-ended one. [source](https://reachkit.app/)
7. **Check your weekly movement email.** Every Monday you see what moved, which is how you track whether the new pages are changing your numbers over time.
8. **Let your market get re-measured weekly.** Your whole market is re-measured weekly, which keeps your score current as rivals publish their own content and AI answers shift.

That sequence — scan, pick rivals, read the score, publish, review, go live, check weekly — is what moves a business from absent to named. Each step depends on the one before it: a wrong rival list skews the score, a skipped review lets an unchecked page stand in for your own words, and a missed weekly check means you find out late rather than early. Nothing in the facts here points to a faster shortcut, and inventing one wouldn't help you.

## How do you check it's working?

Check two numbers over time: your Discoverability Score and your AI answers count. If both move up week over week, the work is landing; if they sit flat, something in your market or your pages needs attention.

The weekly movement email is built for this — it's sent every Monday so you see what moved without having to log in and compare manually. Alongside it, your market gets re-measured weekly, so the score you're watching reflects current conditions, not a snapshot from when you started.

A practical habit: open the email each Monday, note the Discoverability Score and the AI answers fraction (for example, 2 out of 12), and compare it to the week before. A rising score with a flat AI answers count tells you Google ranking is moving faster than AI mentions — useful to know, since the two don't always move together. Treat the two numbers as separate signals rather than one combined score: a page can lift your ranking in search while an AI answer still names only your rivals, and the gap between those two outcomes is exactly what the weekly check is for.

## What mistakes should you avoid?

The most common mistake is skipping the scan and guessing at what to publish — without it, you don't know which questions already exclude you, so you can't target them. The scan exists precisely to replace that guesswork with a number.

Other mistakes to watch for:

- **Publishing without reviewing.** The 24-hour veto window exists so you read a page before it goes live — skip that check and you might let something out that misrepresents your own facts.
- **Checking once and stopping.** A single scan or a single published page won't hold a position, since rivals keep publishing too — that's why the weekly re-measurement and movement email exist.
- **Picking the wrong rivals.** The market and rivals step is suggested for you but meant to be confirmed, not accepted blindly — if your real competitors differ from the suggestion, the whole comparison drifts.
- **Ignoring the AI answers count.** It's easy to watch only the Discoverability Score and miss that AI answers can lag behind — both numbers matter, and they don't always rise together.
- **Treating the first page as the finish line.** One page changes one answer at best; the gap buyers see across a whole market closes only as more of the questions that name your rivals get answered from your own site, one page at a time.
